import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Chebyshev
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sqrt
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds
import Definitions.Def_AbcAdaptation_Reference_Iut_Implication_PrimeSelection

namespace AbcAdaptation.Reference


/-!
# Prime selection for Corollary 2.2 (IUT IV, Proposition 2.1(ii) and (P1)–(P3))

The proof of IUT IV, Corollary 2.2 chooses, for an elliptic curve `E_F` of height
`h = log(q_∀)`, a prime `ℓ` such that

* (P1) `√h ≤ ℓ ≤ 10δ·√h·log(2δh)`;
* (P2) `ℓ` divides no nonzero local height `h_v`;
* (P3) if `ℓ = p_v` for some bad place `v` then `h_v < √h`.

The tool is IUT IV, Proposition 2.1(ii): from Chebyshev-type bounds `(2/3)x ≤ θ(x) ≤ 2x`
for `x ≥ ξ_prm`, for every finite set `A` of primes there is a prime `p ∉ A` with
`p ≤ 2(θ_A + ξ_prm)`, where `θ_A = ∑_{p ∈ A} log p`. The Chebyshev bounds themselves are
the explicit certificate `ChebyshevBound` (taxis #6), discharged from Mathlib in
`ChebyshevExplicit.lean` (`chebyshevBoundExplicit`); everything else in this file is proved.

The local heights enter through `LocalHeightData`: a finite family of bad places with
residue characteristics `p_v`, local heights `h_v ≥ 1`, and residue degrees `f_v ≥ 1`,
with `[F : ℚ]·h = ∑_v h_v·f_v·log p_v` and `[F : ℚ] ≤ δ` — the data of the `q`-divisor
of `E_F` in the notation of IUT IV, Theorem 1.10 and [GenEll], Definition 3.3.
-/

universe w

namespace Iut

open Finset Real















namespace ChebyshevBound

variable (cheb : ChebyshevBound)



end ChebyshevBound



namespace LocalHeightData

variable (L : LocalHeightData)

















end LocalHeightData

end Iut

end AbcAdaptation.Reference

open AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut
open AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.LocalHeightData
open Finset Real
variable (L : LocalHeightData)
payload.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.LocalHeightData.exists_prime_selection (cheb : ChebyshevBound) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 2 ≤ δ)
    (hdeg : (L.deg : ℝ) ≤ δ) (hξ : cheb.ξ ≤ Real.sqrt L.height) :
    ∃ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ Real.sqrt L.height ≤ ℓ ∧
      (ℓ : ℝ) ≤ 10 * δ * Real.sqrt L.height * Real.log (2 * δ * L.height) ∧
      (∀ v ∈ L.bad, ¬ ℓ ∣ L.hv v) ∧
      (∀ v ∈ L.bad, L.p v = ℓ → (L.hv v : ℝ) < Real.sqrt L.height) := by
  sorry
payload.theorem_title: A prime adapted to finite local-height data
payload.natural_language_statement:
**English**

At an arbitrary universe level $w$, let $L$ be any datum consisting of a type $\iota$ in $\mathrm{Type}\,w$, a finite subset $B\subseteq\iota$, three functions $p,h_v,f:\iota\to\mathbb N$, and a natural number $d\ge1$, with the following conditions: for every $v\in B$, $p(v)$ is prime, $h_v(v)\ge1$, and $f(v)\ge1$; and for every natural number $q$, $\sum_{v\in B,\ p(v)=q} f(v)\le d$. The type $\iota$ need not be finite, the functions have no additional restrictions outside $B$, and different members of $B$ may have the same value of $p$. Define the real number $h=\frac1d\sum_{v\in B}h_v(v)f(v)\log p(v)$, where $\log$ is the real natural logarithm and all natural numbers in real expressions are embedded in $\mathbb R$. For every datum $\mathrm{cheb}$ consisting of a real $\xi\ge5$ with $\frac23x\le\theta(x)\le2x$ for every real $x\ge\xi$, where $\theta(x)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb N,\ p\text{ prime},\ p\le x}\log p$, and for every real number $\delta$ satisfying $2\le\delta$, $d\le\delta$, and $\xi\le\sqrt h$, there exists a natural number $\ell$ such that $\ell$ is prime, $\sqrt h\le\ell\le10\delta\sqrt h\log(2\delta h)$, $\ell\nmid h_v(v)$ for every $v\in B$, and $h_v(v)<\sqrt h$ for every $v\in B$ with $p(v)=\ell$. Here $\sqrt h$ is the nonnegative real square root; the hypotheses imply $h\ge25$, so the denominator $d$ and logarithm argument $2\delta h$ are positive. Although the data structure permits $B=\varnothing$ (then $h=0$), such data do not satisfy $\xi\le\sqrt h$. The coefficient $10$ applies to all these inputs; the prime is quantified after $L$, $\mathrm{cheb}$, and $\delta$, with no uniqueness assertion. The quantified input consists of the specified data and their formula-defined $h$; neither a number field nor a curve is a quantified object or an existential conclusion.

**简体中文**

任取宇宙层级 $w$，设 $L$ 是这样一份数据：一个属于 $\mathrm{Type}\,w$ 的类型 $\iota$、一个有限子集 $B\subseteq\iota$、三个函数 $p,h_v,f:\iota\to\mathbb N$，以及一个自然数 $d\ge1$；它们满足：对每个 $v\in B$，$p(v)$ 是素数，$h_v(v)\ge1$，且 $f(v)\ge1$；对每个自然数 $q$，有 $\sum_{v\in B,\ p(v)=q} f(v)\le d$。类型 $\iota$ 不必有限；这三个函数在 $B$ 外没有其他限制，$B$ 中的不同元素也可以具有相同的 $p$ 值。定义实数 $h=\frac1d\sum_{v\in B}h_v(v)f(v)\log p(v)$，其中 $\log$ 是实自然对数，实数表达式中的自然数均按其对应实数理解。对每一份数据 $\mathrm{cheb}$，它给出一个实数 $\xi\ge5$，并使每个实数 $x\ge\xi$ 都满足 $\frac23x\le\theta(x)\le2x$，其中 $\theta(x)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb N,\ p\text{ 为素数},\ p\le x}\log p$；再对每个满足 $2\le\delta$、$d\le\delta$ 和 $\xi\le\sqrt h$ 的实数 $\delta$，都存在自然数 $\ell$，使得 $\ell$ 是素数，$\sqrt h\le\ell\le10\delta\sqrt h\log(2\delta h)$，对每个 $v\in B$ 都有 $\ell\nmid h_v(v)$，并且对每个满足 $p(v)=\ell$ 的 $v\in B$ 都有 $h_v(v)<\sqrt h$。这里 $\sqrt h$ 是非负实平方根；前提蕴含 $h\ge25$，所以分母 $d$ 和对数真数 $2\delta h$ 均为正。数据结构允许 $B=\varnothing$，此时 $h=0$，但这样的数据不满足 $\xi\le\sqrt h$。系数 $10$ 对所有这些输入一致适用；素数的量词位于 $L$、$\mathrm{cheb}$ 和 $\delta$ 之后，结论不要求唯一性。所量化的输入就是上述数据及按公式计算的 $h$；数域和曲线均不在量化对象或存在性结论之中。

**日本語**

任意の宇宙レベル $w$ において、$L$ を次のデータとする。すなわち、$\mathrm{Type}\,w$ に属する型 $\iota$、有限部分集合 $B\subseteq\iota$、三つの関数 $p,h_v,f:\iota\to\mathbb N$、および自然数 $d\ge1$ からなり、すべての $v\in B$ に対して $p(v)$ が素数、$h_v(v)\ge1$、$f(v)\ge1$ であり、すべての自然数 $q$ に対して $\sum_{v\in B,\ p(v)=q}f(v)\le d$ を満たすものとする。型 $\iota$ 自体が有限である必要はなく、三つの関数には $B$ の外で追加の制約はなく、$B$ の異なる要素が同じ $p$ の値を持つことも許される。実数 $h=\frac1d\sum_{v\in B}h_v(v)f(v)\log p(v)$ を定義する。ここで $\log$ は実数の自然対数であり、実数の式に現れる自然数は実数に埋め込んで解釈する。実数 $\xi\ge5$ と、すべての実数 $x\ge\xi$ に対する評価 $\frac23x\le\theta(x)\le2x$ からなる任意のデータ $\mathrm{cheb}$ を与える。ただし $\theta(x)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb N,\ p\text{ は素数},\ p\le x}\log p$ である。このとき、$2\le\delta$、$d\le\delta$、$\xi\le\sqrt h$ を満たすすべての実数 $\delta$ に対して、素数である自然数 $\ell$ が存在し、$\sqrt h\le\ell\le10\delta\sqrt h\log(2\delta h)$、すべての $v\in B$ に対する $\ell\nmid h_v(v)$、および $p(v)=\ell$ を満たすすべての $v\in B$ に対する $h_v(v)<\sqrt h$ が成り立つ。$\sqrt h$ は非負の実平方根である。仮定から $h\ge25$ が従うため、分母 $d$ と対数の引数 $2\delta h$ は正である。データ構造は $B=\varnothing$ も許し、その場合 $h=0$ となるが、このデータは $\xi\le\sqrt h$ を満たさない。係数 $10$ はこれらすべての入力に共通であり、素数の量化は $L$、$\mathrm{cheb}$、$\delta$ の後に置かれる。一意性は主張しない。量化される入力は上記のデータと式によって計算される $h$ であり、数体も曲線も量化対象または存在結論には含まれない。

**Paper source context (English)**

The original source is Mochizuki, IUT IV, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), printed/PDF pp. 44–45, especially (P1)–(P3) on p. 45. On p. 44 the paper writes h = log(q_∀) = [F:ℚ]^(−1)∑_v h_v f_v log(p_v), with h_v = 0 at good reduction and positive integral h_v at bad multiplicative reduction, assumes √h ≥ ξ_prm ≥ 5 after enlarging the finite exceptional set, and uses [F:ℚ] ≤ δ. It bounds the sums of log(p_v) and log(h_v) over places with h_v ≥ √h. The excluded finite set A consists of primes p satisfying one of (S1) p ≤ √h, (S2) p divides a nonzero h_v, or (S3) p = p_v at a place with h_v ≥ √h. Page 45 gives θ_A ≤ 2√h + δ√h + 2δ√h log(2δh) ≤ 4δ√h log(2δh) ≤ −ξ_prm + 5δ√h log(2δh). Applying Proposition 2.1 yields a prime ℓ satisfying (P1) √h ≤ ℓ ≤ 10δ√h log(2δh), (P2) ℓ divides no nonzero h_v, and (P3) h_v < √h whenever p_v = ℓ. These three conditions are the direct paper source for the prime-selection node.

The node is implemented in refer/iut/Iut/Implication/PrimeSelection.lean:213. The code uses the supplied finite LocalHeightData package; it does not construct elliptic-curve local heights. Its exclusion set stores prime factors and residue characteristics only for places with h_v ≥ √h, in addition to the primes ≤ √h. The remaining small positive h_v cannot have a prime divisor ℓ > √h. This is a finite-set implementation of the paper’s exclusion argument. The coefficient 2 in the code’s upper Chebyshev bound differs from the printed 4/3, while the paper’s displayed θ_A estimate on p. 45 already uses 2√h for the small-prime contribution. The output retains the first two bounds of (P1) and conditions (P2), (P3); the additional elementary upper estimate 20δ²h² is printed in (P1) but is not a conclusion field of this node.
